To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
post-growth annealings cause both the structural and magnetic ordering temperatures of BaFe2AS2 to increase, sharpen, and converge.

annealing causes: (1) the structural and magnetic transition temperatures to increase, sharpen, and converge; (2) the c-axis lattice constant to increase for short annealing times, but to remain constant for longer anneal times; and (3) the structural transition to become first-order-like when the magnetic and the structural transition temperatures coincide, and second-order-like when the temperatures are separated.

annealing BaFe2As 2 at temperatures between 600 and 700 °C causes the structural and magnetic phase transitions to become concurrent in temperature, and that the structural transition becomes first order like when the two transitions occur simultaneously.
